SCENE (chosen):
Free design — you design this scene yourself: the place, the activity, her pose, the composition and the outfit. Start from this character's own traits — her species, type and personality — and show one everyday moment that is unexpected, yet feels natural for her. Make it fresh through the situation and what she is doing, not through more decoration. In your pose, give each hand one job only and say plainly where each arm goes; avoid poses where it is unclear which shoulder an arm comes from — an arm behind her back, behind her head or pinned under her body — and never state where a foot sits under water.
Avoid scenes similar to our recent work: the other casual cuts in this pack (casual*-prompt.txt) and every cut you have drawn earlier in this session — choose a different kind of place, activity, pose and framing. Do not make it another small repair, adjusting, measuring or sorting task at a workbench, repair stall, equipment room or locker room — those scenes are already in our own list; choose another kind of everyday moment (rest, play, a meal, travel, weather, getting ready, simply being in the place).
Outfit (yours): create a revealing, fashionable outfit for the moment you design, as daring as the scene allows: a figure-hugging cut with bare skin by design (neckline, shoulders, midriff or legs), styled with care. Before drawing, read our outfit catalog (outfit-catalog.md in this pack — every outfit type we already use) and design one that is NOT in it.
Time of day (fixed): an overcast day — soft, shadowless grey-white light — set your scene at this time.
Keep every rule outside this SCENE exactly as written — her face (FACE), the style (STYLE) and the body rules (BODY TYPE, ANATOMY, BODY, HANDS) — and keep the expression and intensity lines below.
EXPRESSION: softly lowered brows, warm relaxed eyes, faint closed-lip smile, no tension anywhere. Show it mildly, only with her brows, eyelids and mouth corners; her face shape and features stay exactly as in the attached image.
overall_intensity: strong — maximal styling presence within the scene; retain chosen exposure and anatomy
skin_exposure: bold — the chosen outfit worn in its most revealing version — a deep neckline with natural cleavage, bare shoulders, a cropped or open-back cut, a short hem or high slit showing the thighs, as far as the outfit allows, skin clearly showing; nothing slipped off; chest and pelvis covered

Do not carry the attached image's palette, patterns or trim into the outfit; her source belongs in accessories and props, never in the clothes — never restyle the chosen outfit into her own costume, genre or palette.

ANGLE: the attached image fixes who she is, not how she is posed or shot. Do not copy its head angle, head tilt, gaze direction, face size in frame, camera height or crop — turn her head, set her gaze and place the camera as SCENE describes, and let her face read naturally from that new angle (profile, three-quarter, looking down or away), with her features staying the same.

ONE MAIN FIGURE: she is the only character in focus; other people may appear only as small, soft-focus background extras — never posed with her. No Pokémon, animals or other creatures, no text, no lettering, no logo, no watermark, no speech bubble, no frame border.

ANATOMY: natural adult proportions — about 7.5 heads tall, her head in proportion to her shoulders and body. No extra limbs; her worn features are costume, never extra limbs.

BODY: a normal human body — one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; elbows, knees and wrists bend the human way. Hands and feet may be partly hidden by the pose, what she holds or the frame. Right and left mean her own right and left, not the viewer's.

HANDS: natural human hands, no extra or duplicated limbs; each visible hand joins through its wrist and forearm to the matching shoulder. A hand may leave the frame past the forearm, never floating without its arm; fingers may be partly hidden by a grip.
